title: Kenyan Creamy Garlic Chicken
localName: Kuku wa Cream ya Vitunguu Saumu
community: Urban Kenya — the hotel and restaurant crowd-pleaser
author: Chef Amina Hassan
desc: Kenyan Creamy Garlic Chicken — pan-seared chicken breasts in a rich cream sauce with roasted garlic, fresh herbs, and a hint of paprika. The most popular chicken dish in Nairobi's hotel restaurants — universally adored and genuinely excellent.
longDesc: Creamy garlic chicken is the dish that appears on every Nairobi hotel menu for good reason — the combination of properly seared chicken and a rich, garlicky cream sauce satisfies in a way that simpler preparations do not. The Kenyan version adds paprika and fresh coriander for character.
steps: Season chicken with salt, paprika, and pepper.
Heat oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken for 4—5 minutes per side until golden. Remove.
Reduce heat. Add butter and garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add stock. Deglaze, scraping up any browned bits.
Add cream, mustard, and paprika. Bring to a simmer.
Simmer covered for 10—12 minutes until chicken is cooked through.
Add lemon juice and coriander. Serve.
chefTips: Do not move the chicken during searing — this is how the golden crust develops.
Deglaze thoroughly — the browned bits are the most flavourful part of the pan.
Add lemon juice only at the end — acid in the cream sauce too early can cause curdling.
commonMistakes: Boiling the cream sauce vigorously — it breaks.
cookingScience: The fond (browned bits) left in the pan after searing is a concentrate of Maillard-reaction products. Deglazing with stock dissolves these compounds into the sauce, providing a depth of flavour that a cream sauce made without the searing step cannot replicate.
sustainabilityTips: Free-range Kenyan chicken gives the best flavour and texture for this dish.
reheating: Gently on stovetop with splash of cream.
healthBenefits: Best enjoyed as a restaurant treat.
culturalNote: Creamy garlic chicken represents Nairobi's hotel and restaurant scene at its most crowd-pleasing — a dish that satisfies every table while showcasing the quality of Kenyan poultry and the skill of a properly trained kitchen.
